name: craftsman-marketplace
description: Practical, opinionated craft skills for Claude Code and Codex: engineering-readiness audits for AI-built apps, and CPA-grade US tax and accounting workpapers.

plugins.name: craftsman
plugins.description: Ship something with Lovable, Replit, Bolt, v0, Claude Code, or Codex and it works, but nobody with an engineering background has checked it before real customers arrive. craft-audit reviews the whole project the way a senior engineer would, across ten areas: not just security, but the database rules that keep one customer's data separate from another's, whether the money path is tested, and whether errors get seen before a customer has to report them. Findings are plain language, ranked by real consequence, so a broken invoice check beats a missing comment, and written to a workspace in your project so a long audit can pause and resume. The companion skill craft-fix drives the repairs but can never mark its own work fixed; only a fresh audit pass confirms that. A full worked example is included, so you can see exactly what it finds before you run it. Not a penetration test, not continuous monitoring, no numeric score.

plugins.name: taxcraft
plugins.description: US tax and accounting work for people whose situation outgrew consumer tax software but who still do the prep themselves: multiple entities, K-1s that arrive late and wrong, basis and carryforwards nobody is tracking, quarterly estimates guessed at rather than computed. It builds the workpapers a CPA would build — transaction-level books from raw statements and CSVs, reconciled balance sheets, partner and shareholder basis, capital-loss and NOL and passive and QBI carryforwards, 1040-ES and corporate estimates under the annualized income method — and shows the math with the Code section behind it. Covers 1040, 1065, 1120-S, 1120, disregarded SMLLCs, and corporate governance records: bylaws, minutes, consents, annual reports, stock issuances. Each year's numbers come from a dated rules file, so a prior year never silently answers a current-year question. It does not file returns and it is not tax advice: estimates, workpapers, and drafts for a licensed CPA, EA, or attorney to verify before you rely on them.
